flags: arm dead: CONSTANT_PREDICTION
split: evaluation keys overlap training (1.000)

the_danger_it_introduces.what_happens: the masked identity block is declared expected, so the audit passes. But that block still enters the model and still consumes splits, which is precisely the defect that cost two rounds to find in R147 and R148.
the_danger_it_introduces.so: the whitelist buys quiet at the price of trusting the declaration of intent, and intent declarations can be wrong

what_still_works.prediction_level: a constant arm is still flagged with the whitelist in place
what_still_works.split_level: training and evaluation overlap is still flagged with the whitelist in place
what_still_works.scope: suppression is confined to feature-level flags on the named columns

limits: Intent declarations are the operator's, and they can be wrong.
Only feature-level flags can be suppressed; that is by design.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.

bug_1.what: CONSTANT_ON_EVAL fired for every level simply absent from the evaluation sample
bug_1.why_it_matters: in a 65-drug one-hot design that is most columns, so the check was mostly noise
bug_1.fix: it now requires the constant value to be NON-ZERO, which is what a filled-in placeholder looks like

bug_2.why_it_matters: a one-hot column for a drug absent from evaluation never contains that drug's value in training either, so it reported unseen codes purely as sampling
bug_2.fix: the unseen-code test now applies only to genuine multi-level code columns

bug_3.what: a PARTIALLY masked column slipped through both checks
bug_3.why_it_matters: masking -1 on some rows and 0 on others is neither constant nor an unseen code on an indicator column, and that is precisely the shape of the R138 defect
bug_3.fix: a new SENTINEL_OUTSIDE_VOCAB check flags any value outside {0,1} in an indicator column

three_real_bugs_in_my_own_audit_were_fou.how_they_were_found: R157's design went through the audit and flagged all four arms; chasing that false alarm one case at a time produced these three fixes

the_whitelist_and_its_danger.what_it_does: suppresses FEATURE-level flags only, and only on columns the caller names as expected to be uninformative
the_whitelist_and_its_danger.what_it_cannot_do: prediction-level and split-level alarms still fire with the whitelist in place, because neither can be intentional

the_danger_demonstrated.case_3: a design masking the held drug's column to -1, no whitelist: correctly FLAGGED
the_danger_demonstrated.case_4: the SAME design with those columns declared expected: PASSES
the_danger_demonstrated.so: the whitelist buys quiet at the price of trusting the declaration of intent, and R138 is a case where that declaration looked reasonable and the design was still broken

the_whitelist_and_its_danger.recommendation: never whitelist a block whose purpose is to simulate an unavailable feature; whitelist only blocks that are unavailable by construction

what_this_means_for_R157: the all-four-arms flag in R157 was mostly the CONSTANT_ON_EVAL noise described above, not a defect in that design. Under the corrected rules the R157 design passes cleanly.
